title: Stage B: P_2=h^0(2K) identified with module degree-0 piece, not saturated cohomology

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Stage B (Lemma `lem:cohomology`): $P_2=h^0(2K_S)$ is identified with the degree-0 piece of a presenting module, not with sheaf cohomology.**

The proof computes $P_2(S)=\dim_k(\Omega^{(2)})_{\deg 0}$ "in the sheafified sense". For a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathrm{Proj}\,R$, $h^0(\mathcal{F})$ equals the degree-0 part of the **saturated** module (equivalently read off the BGG/Tate resolution), which in general differs from the degree-0 piece of an arbitrary presenting module $\Omega^{(2)}$ by the submodule $H^0_{\mathfrak{m}}$ (saturation). The text does not specify that saturation / the Tate output is used.

Also, the "double-dual / reflexive hull of $\Omega\otimes_R\Omega$" language is unnecessary and slightly misleading: on a *smooth* surface $\omega_S$ is invertible, so $\omega_S^{\otimes 2}$ is already locally free and its module is computed directly.

This is the mildest of the gaps (borderline between a genuine gap and a citable standard fact), but the identification $P_2=(\text{module})_{\deg 0}$ should be replaced by an explicit "$=$ degree-0 part of the saturated module / Tate resolution of $\omega_S^{\otimes 2}$" to be rigorous.
